name: Bouillon/stock cubes and powdered seasoning blends (dry rubs, gravy/seasoning packets)
native_basis_label: dry seasoning blend as placed on the market (dry)
scope_note: Covers bouillon/stock cubes and powdered seasoning blends (dry rubs, gravy and seasoning packets). No sovereign sets a blend-specific ML, so lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury read across the nearest applicable sovereign scope — the spice-blend / curry-powder limits (curry powder is the archetypal, explicitly-regulated seasoning blend). Chromium is screened as a lead-chromate adulteration co-marker for chili/paprika-forward blends. Salt-dominant bouillon cubes additionally sit at or below the food-grade-salt lead ceiling.

Cd.basis: food as listed; source unit mg/kg or mg/l
Cd.label: read across the spice-blend / curry-powder scope (Vietnam cadmium 1000 ug/kg); nearest applicable sovereign for a dry seasoning blend.

tAs.label: read across the curry-powder scope (Singapore total arsenic 1000 ug/kg; Vietnam curry powder concurs at 1000); curry powder is the archetypal seasoning blend.

tHg.basis: food as listed; source unit mg/kg or mg/l
tHg.label: read across the spice-blend / curry-powder scope (Vietnam total mercury 50 ug/kg); nearest applicable sovereign for a dry seasoning blend.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is the organomercury speciation of mercury and is arithmetically bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg); a dry seasoning blend of spices, salt and starch has no methylmercury formation pathway, and it is bounded by the read-across total-mercury limit.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the read-across total-Hg standard (50); no methylmercury blend ML anywhere

Ni.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a nickel maximum level for seasoning blends or spices. Screened rather than assigned an invented or mis-based number.
Ni.reference_method: Total-nickel screen (ICP-MS); no sovereign blend/spice nickel ML.
Ni.trigger: periodic nickel screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Sn.rationale: No tin source in a foil/pouched dry seasoning blend or a stock cube; tin is a tinplate-can migration pathway only.
Sn.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); periodic ICP-MS tin verification.
Sn.regulatory_basis: No dry-blend tin ML; canned-food 250 mg/kg limit is can-only

Al.rationale: A seasoning blend is compositionally spices plus salt; its aluminium is the natural-accumulator spice background plus permitted anti-caking additive, managed by intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI and by additive law, not by a per-food contaminant maximum level. Consistent with the spices/Al and salt/Al determinations.
Al.reference_method: Managed by intake vs TWI + additive law; periodic screen.
Al.regulatory_basis: No Al contaminant ML for seasoning blends; managed by TWI + additive law
Al.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (lists no Al); Codex; FSANZ; JECFA/EFSA TWI

Cr.rationale: No total-chromium food maximum level in any jurisdiction. Chili/paprika-forward seasoning blends carry the same lead-chromate adulteration risk as whole spices, so total chromium is screened and co-read with lead as an adulteration co-marker.
Cr.reference_method: Total-chromium screen (ICP-MS), co-read with lead; substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
Cr.trigger: flag when total chromium is elevated and co-occurs with elevated lead (lead-chromate adulteration signature)

Cr-VI.rationale: Chili/paprika seasoning blends can carry lead-chromate (hexavalent-chromium) adulteration, so Cr-VI is screened, not dismissed. Reflex Cr-VI speciation confirms the chromate where the lead/total-chromium screen is elevated. No sovereign Cr-VI food ML exists.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Reflex Cr-VI speciation on the lead-chromate adulteration signature.
Cr-VI.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation on the lead-chromate adulteration signature

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; explicit-id lookup; legislated product-form splits preserved; dried-spice basis discipline)
